what_happened: While turning right at the intersection, the ego kept creeping forward and sped up slightly (2.7 to 3.2 m/s) as a dark car (actor 112) crossed in front of it and turned onto the same street. The ego's front hit the side of that car as the car straightened into the near lane. The ego never yielded, even though the car was clearly visible on the camera crossing its planned path.

After the handoff at 4.7 s, the ego kept going about 12 m/s and steered left into the next lane, where vehicle 2 was. It hit that car with its front at 6.7 s. The recorded human went straight and then drifted right as the route command changed to RIGHT.

The ego was going about 12 m/s in the right lane, and the recorded route bore right. Instead, the policy's planned path cut left into the next lane, where actor 2 was driving just ahead on the ego's left. The ego merged into that lane without slowing and hit actor 2 with its front at 6.7 s.

At about 12 m/s on a straight multi-lane road, the ego's planned path drifted left from its right-hand lane into the next lane, where car 2 was driving just ahead and to the left. The ego cut into that car's lane without slowing and its front hit car 2 at 6.7 s, about 1.5 m left of the recorded human path, which stayed right (the route command turned to RIGHT).

The ego was going straight at about 12 m/s in the right lane and its plan steered left toward the next lane, where vehicle 2 was driving slightly ahead. The ego drifted across the lane line without slowing, and its front hit the rear quarter of vehicle 2 at 6.7 s (gap to vehicle 2 fell from 27.5 m to 4.5 m).

At about 3 m/s in the intersection, with a RIGHT route command, the ego left the green route and swung left toward the curb lane of the cross street. Its front ran into parked car 90 at the curb, and it also went off the drivable area. Car 111, following behind, made rear contact, but the front collision came first.

The ego crept into the intersection at a steady 2.6 m/s to make its right turn and never slowed for actor 112. That dark sedan was crossing in front of it through the intersection and was clearly visible in the camera for about two seconds. The ego's front hit the side of 112 at 9.6 s, about 3.9 m ahead of where the human driver was at that moment, which suggests the recorded human waited for the car to pass.

The route turns right at the intersection, but after handoff the policy planned straight and slightly left. At the stop line the ego was flagged offroad while only 0.8 m from the human trajectory and not visibly near a black road edge on the map. The flag likely comes from a tight drivable-area boundary (possibly the lane or tram-track edge on the left), not from a clear departure from the road.

The ego entered a signalized intersection at about 9 m/s on a green light and held a straight plan. The route turned right, but the command showed STRAIGHT until the failure frame. At 6.2 s it was flagged offroad at the intersection entry while only 0.7 m from the human's path, so this looks like a marginal clip of the drivable-area boundary, possibly from a map artifact, rather than a clear departure.

The ego was entering an intersection at about 9 m/s. The route path curves right, but the command showed STRAIGHT until the last frame, and the policy planned straight on and slightly left (orange path). It was flagged offroad just past the stop line, only about 0.7 m off the recorded trajectory, while its box still looks to be inside the mapped lanes. That makes this a marginal offroad flag, possibly a quirk of how the map defines the drivable area in the intersection.

As the ego reached the stop line of a signalized intersection (green light, lead car about 29 m ahead), it kept heading straight at about 9 m/s. The route wanted a right turn there: the command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT only at 6.2 s, and the ego was flagged offroad at the stop line, where its lane starts to curve right. The ego was only 0.7 m from the recorded human path, so this looks like a marginal clip of the drivable-area edge, possibly made worse by the late route command and the map geometry, not a clear drift off the road.

The ego stayed in its lane behind white car 99 as it approached the intersection, and did not take the recorded rightward path. Car 99 slowed almost to a stop, closing the gap at about 11 m/s, from 34 m to 0.6 m in 3 s. The ego only eased from 13 to 9.6 m/s and hit 99's rear with its front.

Going straight through the intersection at about 9 m/s, the ego drifted about 1.7 m left of the recorded path toward the adjacent left lane. Its front clipped actor 33, which was travelling alongside it in that lane. No lead vehicle had stopped ahead; the collision came from the ego's lateral drift into the neighbouring car.

On a narrow residential street lined with parked cars, the ego kept going about 13–14 m/s and edged left toward the parked cars on the left, about 1.9 m off the recorded path. A parked car (actor 6) ended up straight ahead of it, and the gap shrank from 32 m to 1.5 m while the ego only slowed to 12.3 m/s, so its front hit the car at 7.1 s, just before a right turn at the intersection ahead.

On a narrow residential street, with a right turn coming up, the ego drifted left toward the line of parked cars instead of moving right. It kept going at 12–14 m/s and drove its front into parked car 6, which had been in its path and closing from 32 m to 1.7 m, without braking enough to stop.

After handoff, the ego kept going straight at about 12–14 m/s down a narrow residential street with cars parked on both sides. It drifted toward the left curb and its front corner clipped parked car 6 at 7.1 s, as it reached the intersection where the route says turn right. It hit a static parked car without turning and while still on the road, so none of the listed causes fits.

The route called for a right turn at the upcoming intersection, but after handoff the policy drifted left toward the line of cars parked on the left curb. Still doing about 12 m/s, it clipped parked car 6 with its front-left corner at 7.1 s.

The route said to turn RIGHT, but the policy went straight. It drifted left to straddle the lane line and closed on white car 99 ahead, which was nearly stopped, while only easing off from 12.9 to 10.0 m/s. The gap shrank from 34 m to 0.5 m and the ego's front-left hit the car's rear-left at 9.1 s. The rear contact recorded in this run did not cause the failure.

The command was RIGHT, but the ego went straight toward the intersection, straddling the lane line instead of moving right as the recorded driver did. It closed on the slow, nearly stopped white car 99 just ahead-left at about 10–12 m/s while braking only lightly (12.9→10.0 m/s). The gap fell from 34 m to 0.9 m, and the ego's front clipped 99's rear corner.

The ego stayed in the left lane behind a slowing white sedan (actor 99), even though the route said RIGHT and the recorded human path moved one lane right. Over 3 s the gap shrank from 34 m to 2 m while the ego only eased from 13 to 8.6 m/s, and its front hit the sedan at 9.1 s.

The command was STRAIGHT, and the ego was crossing the intersection at about 9 m/s. Its planned path bent left, so it drifted about 1.5 m left of the recorded line and into the side of vehicle 33, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane; the lead car (34) was still about 20 m ahead.

While driving straight through the intersection at about 9.5 m/s, the ego's planned path (orange) drifted left of the recorded human path (green). By 8.7 s the ego was 1.7 m off the recording and sideswiped actor 33, which was traveling alongside in the adjacent left lane (a lateral at-fault collision; there was no front or rear contact).

The route said RIGHT, but the ego ignored it and kept going straight toward the intersection while drifting left onto the lane line. It closed on the slow white car (actor 99) that was ahead and partly in its lane, at about 11 m/s relative speed (gap 34 m → 10.8 m in 2 s), and eased off only from 13 to 10.4 m/s. Its front then clipped the car at 9.1 s.

The ego was told to turn RIGHT but kept going nearly straight at about 11–13 m/s and caught up with a slower white car (actor 99) ahead. That car partly overlapped the ego's path along the lane line, and the gap shrank from 34 m to 11 m. The ego barely slowed and tried to squeeze past instead of braking or moving right, and clipped 99's side as it drew level at 9.1 s.

The route said RIGHT and the human driver moved over into the right-turn lane. The ego stayed in its lane and drove up on the slow or stopped white car 99 ahead, closing from 40 m to 4 m at about 12 m/s while slowing only from 13.3 to 11.6 m/s, and hit it with its front. The ego was also hit from behind later, but that came after the frontal collision.

The command was STRAIGHT through the Fourth St intersection. The ego drifted about 1.4 m left of the recorded human path, and its planned path bent left. It side-swiped vehicle 33, which was driving alongside in the adjacent left lane, a lateral collision at about 9 m/s. The lead vehicle stayed about 19 m ahead and played no part.

The ego approached the intersection at about 7 m/s, with the lead car about 30 m ahead. Its plan bent straight-left across the intersection, while the route (command STRAIGHT, then RIGHT) and the recorded trajectory curve right. At 6.2 s, near the stop line, it was flagged offroad only 0.85 m from the human path. The deviation is so small that it could be a marginal crossing of the map's drivable edge rather than a clear drift off the road.
